facts.statement: The holotype fossil of Jakapil was discovered in 2012 and excavated between 2014 and 2019/2020 from land owned by the Mariluan family.
facts.quote: The holotype, MPCA-PV-630, is a partial skeleton including several osteoderms and a complete lower jaw, which were found on land owned by the Mariluan family in 2012 and excavated between 2014 and 2019/2020.

facts.statement: The genus name Jakapil comes from a Puelchean word meaning "shield bearer".
facts.quote: The generic name, "Jakapil", is derived from "Ja-Kapïl", a Puelchean word meaning "shield bearer".

facts.statement: The species name kaniukura means "crest stone" in Mapudungun, referring to the animal's uniquely deep jaw.
facts.quote: The specific name, "kaniukura", means "crest stone" in Mapudungun, in reference to its uniquely deep jaw.

facts.statement: Based on femoral circumference, Jakapil is estimated to be less than 1.5 meters long and weigh between 4.5 and 7 kilograms.
facts.quote: Its describers estimate it to be less than 1.5 m long and 4.5 - 7 kg in weight, based on femoral circumference.

facts.statement: Jakapil had a short robust skull lacking an antorbital fenestra and possessed only 11 pairs of leaf-shaped teeth in the lower jaw without a dental cingulum.
facts.quote: Jakapil poseía un cráneo corto y robusto, carecía una fenestra anterorbital y poseía tan solo 11 pares de dientes en la mandíbula inferior, un número reducido para tireóforos no anquilosáuridos, sus dientes tenían formas de hoja y carecían un cíngulo.

facts.statement: Jakapil's body was covered in at least five types of osteoderms, including large D-shaped ones on the neck sides, spine-like ones on top, intermediate ones below, and small oval ones on the back.
facts.quote: Los laterales del cuello, grandes, con poca elevación y forma de D, los encima del cuello, largas y puntiagudas, similar a una espina, los de debajo del cuello, un punto intermedio entre las dos previas, elevada y gruesa pero no puntiguda. Los de la espalda, similares a las anteriores pero más pequeñas y del cuerpo, ovaladas, típicas en anquilosaurios.

facts.statement: Researchers suggest Jakapil processed tough plant material via mastication rather than shearing leaves, a hypothesis supported by high wear on its teeth.
facts.quote: In light of its straight, narrow snout, Riguetti and colleagues (2022) suggested that Jakapil did not use its teeth and jaws to shear leaves, but instead likely processed tough plant material via mastication, as evidenced by the high amount of wear on the teeth.

facts.statement: Jakapil lived in the Kokorkom desert, an ancient desert ecosystem with oases typical of the Mid-Cretaceous in western Gondwana.
facts.quote: The Candeleros Formation is interpreted as an ancient desert known as the Kokorkom desert, with some oases in it, and its fossils represent a faunal assemblage typical of Mid-Cretaceous ecosystems in the western remnants of Gondwana.

facts.statement: Jakapil lived during the mid-Cretaceous, approximately 97 to 94 million years ago, in what is now South America.
facts.quote: Jakapil kaniukura es la única especie conocida del género extinto Jakapil de dinosaurio tireóforo basal, que vivió a mediados del período Cretácico, hace aproximadamente entre 97 y 94 millones de años, en lo que hoy es Sudamérica.

facts.statement: Fossil records place Jakapil in the Albian stage, between 113.2 and 110.1 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Albian to Albian (113.2 to 110.1 million years ago)

facts.statement: Some researchers dispute Jakapil's classification as a thyreophoran, arguing it possesses unique features not found in other members of the group.
facts.quote: The status of Jakapil as a thyreophoran has been disputed by some researchers; a study focused on the phylogenetic relationships of the Thyreophora noted that the only thyreophoran characteristic it possessed was dermal armor, while presenting features not present in any other thyreophoran.

facts.statement: A study concluded that Jakapil is likely an armored marginocephalian or a member of an unknown lineage of non-thyreophoran ornithischians.
facts.quote: Therefore, the study concluded that Jakapil most likely represents an armored marginocephalian or a member of a yet to be known lineage of non-thyreophoran ornithischians.

facts.statement: In 2024 analyses, Fonseca and colleagues suggested Jakapil could be the sister taxon to Eurypoda or the earliest member of Ankylosauria.
facts.quote: In their 2024 analyses, Fonseca and colleagues recovered Jakapil as either the sister taxon to Eurypoda or as the basalmost member of Ankylosauria.

facts.statement: Jakapil is remarkable for possessing a predentary bone, a feature absent or cartilaginous in other basal thyreophorans.
facts.quote: Jakapil representa un morfotipo novedoso entre los tireóforos, que incluye, entre otras cosas, la presencia de un hueso predentario, ausente o cartilaginoso en otros tireóforos basales, osteodermos grandes y bajos y una postura bípeda, similar a Scutellosaurus.

rejected.statement: Jakapil is characterized by a novel combination of features including a predentary bone, large low osteoderms, and a bipedal stance similar to Scutellosaurus.
rejected.quote: Jakapil represents a novel morphotype among thyreophorans, including, among other things, the presence of a predentary bone (absent or cartilaginous in other basal thyreophorans), large, low osteoderms, and a bipedal stance, similar to Scutellosaurus.
rejected.reason: statement copies the source wording: 'large low osteoderms and a bipedal stance similar'

rejected.statement: Most phylogenetic analyses classify Jakapil as a basal thyreophoran outside the clade Eurypoda.
rejected.quote: Due to a combination of features seen in basal ornithischians, basal thyreophorans, and ankylosaurs, a phylogenetic analysis placed it, according to most data matrices, as a basal thyreophoran, outside the clade Eurypoda.
rejected.reason: statement copies the source wording: 'as a basal thyreophoran outside the clade Eurypoda'

rejected.statement: Although the holotype is not a juvenile, it was likely not fully grown and may not have reached sexual maturity.
rejected.quote: While the holotype remains do not represent a juvenile individual, it was likely not fully grown and may not have been sexually mature.
